The compound crystallizes in a hexagonal cell with lattice parameters a = 9

The structure is an eight-layered hexagonal B-site deficient perovskite with the layer sequence (ccch) 2 and represents the first example of a hexagonal structure among 5d oxides adopting a twin option
The sample shows spontaneous ferromagnetic magnetization below 430 K with a small saturation moment of 0
This is the highest Curie temperature (T ) reported for any bulk B C perovskite containing only 5d ions at the B site
1 INTRODUCTION Perovskites represent one of most robust and perhaps the most structurally variable classes of oxides

1,2 The basic structure type ABO allows for replacements at A and B sites in different ratios 3 and for a wide variety of stacking sequences of the AO dense packed layers, which results in a 3 vast combinatorial diversity of individual configurations
3 The two ideal types of perovskites feature a cubic (c) or hexagonal (h) stacking sequence of the AO layers, and virtually 3 any combination of c and h sequences is possible
